trickyParts: The mirror handler must run before both deciders in the same transaction. A blocked-by-only edit is an issue.updated whose status did not change, and the engine returns early on exactly that (engine.go's `fact.Seq <= issue.LastDispatchSeq || fact.Status == issue.Status`), so neither decider could have written the row itself. internal/intake/handler_order_test.go pins the order by behaviour: a probe standing where admission stands already sees the row, and the engine alone writes none.

record.Waiting is deliberately unchanged. Dropping a blocked root from the waiting line would make record.TreeLive false for it and turn its children into orphans admitted as roots of their own; the skip lives in promoteHolds and in slotFree's count only.

A tree Legion takes back after it finished and lingered comes back at the admitted phase carrying no run, so startedRun alone did not exempt it, while a never-started child handed over from a finished tree — which the spec requires to stay checked — looks identical afterwards. The distinction exists only inside readmit (whether the tree arriving is the root's own), and the judgement happens later, so it is stored: issues.taken_back.

api.Options.Project is the claim project token, not the Dispatch project key; the mirror is keyed by the latter. The driven run caught release_children reading the wrong one, and the api tests now run under two keys that differ, as a deployment's always do.

The architect skill is 14 bytes under the 50 KiB spill threshold its guard enforces. Writing the new rule into it needed two duplicate-removal trims in the same sections to pay for the additions; the next addition to that file needs a reference file instead.
deviations: The committed plan handoff's specDepartures entry and its answer to gap finding F8 are superseded: the architect ruled that a held child's start tells the architect with the existing child-status notice from a third producer, not with phase-finished, and version 3 of the plan document (dispatch://INFRA-225/artifact/plan-md, decision D7) records it. That is what is built (workflow/effects.go ChildUnblockedNotice). plan.json was not edited — the plan document is the record — and this handoff records no spec departure, since with child-status the spec's words hold as written.

Discovered scope the plan named and the architect approved (D12): packages/daemon/internal/testnats gained LEGION_TEST_NATS_URL and LEGION_TEST_NATS_MONITOR_URL, mirroring the door packages/envoy/cmd/dispatch/multiprocess_test.go already has. Without it the issue's own acceptance proof could not run in a pod with no Docker. The testcontainers path is unchanged for CI.

The spec's exemption of a tree taken back after it finished and lingered was not met by the first implementation, which exempted only an issue carrying a run. It is implemented here with migration 0052 and record.Issue.TakenBack; the test that had been written against the wrong behaviour was inverted.

Round 2 answers the tester's two defects and the third this change's own proof found; the tester's two red tests (TestTheGateOpeningStartsAnAdmittedRootWhateverItsLinksSay, TestABlockedRootThatLeftTheQueueAndCameBackIsStillChecked) pass unmodified and were not touched.

TakenBack's meaning changed under the architect's ruling: it is now 'the issue has stood in a phase of its own', written by Engine.transition as a phase begins and never cleared, rather than 'a root came back through readmit'. Admission.readmit writes it no more. Migration 0052 keeps its column name and gains a backfill for rows already recorded (a phase that carries a run, or a non-architect phases row). Its name stays TakenBack because the tester's red test seeds that field by name.

A third way into the state the architect's invariant forbids was fixed with them: a held child whose blocked-by links a person takes off is held by nothing, and StartUnblockedChildren now starts it (no child-status notice, since no blocker closed). The half of TestAHeldChildStartsWhenItsLastBlockerCloses that pinned the old stuck behaviour was replaced by TestAHeldChildWhoseLinksAreTakenOffStarts.

discoveredComplexity: Four packages of packages/daemon cannot pass in this pod and were verified by reading their failures rather than by a green run: internal/testnats and internal/natsauth need Docker (they start containers with their own authorization, which no environment variable can replace), and internal/launcher's TestAResumeIsToldWhetherItsWorkspaceWasRecreatedSinceItsSessionWasWritten and internal/ompsessions' TestImportRefusesContentNoTextValueHolds fail on this sandbox's filesystem and encoding behaviour. None is touched by this change. Three internal/daemon tests (TestTmuxBootRewritesEveryOlderClonesCredentialHelper, TestATerminalAttemptLeavesLaterChildrenSIGTTOUsDefault, TestATerminalAttemptIgnoresSIGTSTP) were shown to fail identically at the base commit, with this change's one file in that package reverted. CI runs all of them.
packages/claude-envoy's `queryTmux is bounded even by a tmux that ignores SIGTERM` is flaky under load here: it fails in a full-suite run and passes alone and in a second full run.

Two defects of this change were found by its own proof rather than by review: release_children reading the mirror with the claim project token instead of the Dispatch project key (held was always empty in a deployment), and admission not promoting on an observation of an issue it keeps no record of (the close of such a blocker waited about 58s for the controller tick). Both are fixed, and both have driven coverage.

internal/daemon is close to Go's ten-minute package timeout under load: it hit 600.080s and failed as a timeout while other packages ran beside it, against 510s alone. The driven proof's one-minute wait for the runtime's first controller tick was the cause and is gone (the boot override sets the first tick too), bringing the package to about 469-580s. A tester running the whole module on a loaded machine should know the margin is thin.

This pod has no C compiler, so internal/supervise's type-check tests (TestTheTableHasARowOrANamedIgnoreForEveryEventInEveryState and its two neighbours) fail here with 'go tool cgo: exit status 2' and pass with CGO_ENABLED=0. Nothing of this change touches that package.
